title: Classical guitar
summary: First slice (Gt-S1): one plain nylon treble string at a time (G3, B3, E4) plucked by a load-release gesture, coupled through a bridge spring to a flat rectangular cedar soundboard chart and a Helmholtz cavity, rendered by the generic material_strings example with the prepared exact propagator. It tests the existing string-to-body coupling; it is not yet a guitar body. Each string's tension was set once by the frozen setup protocol (model fundamental tuned to equal temperament, no recording involved). Wound bass strings and the six-string sympathetic network are not rendered yet.
physics_present: Each string is a convergent modal beam in two transverse polarizations, with nylon density and bending modulus from Lynch-Aird and Woodhouse 2017 (harp-string proxy) and gauges from the D'Addario EJ45 specification
Tension is set per string by the setup protocol on the model fundamental (stiff-string fit of the tracked partials), never from a recording
The string couples through a bridge spring to a plane-stress orthotropic cedar plate chart (FPL-GTR-282 constants, viscous loss scenario) and a Helmholtz cavity with a flanged sound hole
Pressure is observed through the compact baffled body and neck monopole at an assumed distance of 1 m
Nylon viscoelastic bending loss from Woodhouse and Lynch-Aird 2019 (Kelvin-Voigt equivalent at 2 kHz)
physics_missing: The six-string network: the three-string files are refused at construction because the bank is built before the prepared propagator is selected, so only the plucked string is rendered and sympathetic strings are absent

String air drag: the published unsteady-Stokes operator exists but its 113-coordinate network is too slow to render with the current propagator, so the only string loss is nylon viscoelastic bending loss, which barely touches the lowest partials; decay is therefore slower than the real strings

Only 12 bending modes per polarization are kept (24 in the m24 convergence files), so partials above a few kHz are absent; the grader fundamental moved by -11.4, -11.2, -10.6 and -5.5 cents (G3, B3, E4, Gb4) from 12 to 24 modes, so the pitch is not converged in the mode count, and the penalty bridge spring acting on the truncated sum adds a narrow line at 7.8 to 14.6 kHz that moves with the mode count
The output is 16-bit PCM at a full scale of 1 Pa: band power above about 3 to 5 kHz is at the PCM16 quantisation floor, so the render cannot show or test any content there

The body is a flat unbraced rectangle with a handful of low modes, not a fan-braced arched guitar top with thickness map, back, ribs and neck; the authored plate size places a mode near B3 that pulls its first partial. A measured plan of ONE real classical-type guitar (a 1964 Madrid guitar, not the Iowa Raimundo 118) now exists as data in data/instruments/geometry/guitar-esteso-1964-zimmer2024 (printed dimensions, thickness points, signature modes A0 98 Hz and T1 200 Hz); no render consumes it yet
Wound bass strings: the multifilament core and silver-plated winding dimensions are unknown
Nylon internal loss, cedar cross-grain and shear loss, and the saddle contact stiffness are unknown; loss is a declared scenario, not a measurement
Finger and nail contact, fret contact for fretted notes, and the player's holding contacts
Radiation is the compact monopole, not a boundary-element microphone with fluid loading
The stretched-string state (the working tension of a real nylon string is below the unstretched-mass value) is not modelled
